newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Police battle student protesters in central Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Police battle student protesters in central Seoul.

text.p: Police fired tear gas at hundreds of South Korean students hurling molotov cocktails on the streets of the capital Seoul on Friday in protest at what they said was suppression of student rights, witnesses said.

The demonstrators took to the streets after a rally on Hanyang University's campus in eastern Seoul to mark the inauguration of the leadership of the Hanchongryon, a militant student body with pro-North Korea sympathies. Police had earlier fired tear gas into the Hanyang campus through the main gate to block students from marching towards the city centre.

Late in the evening, several police helicopters flew low over the campus, targeting search lights across the grounds. Yonhap Television News showed police kicking and beating students with clubs and witnesses said students were shouting "Stop suppressing Hanchongryon" and "Down with the Kim Young-sam government".
There were no immediate reports of casualties.

The students had gathered to express their determination to rebuild the Hanchongryon, which almost collapsed last year after many members were convicted on charges related to campus unrest. Almost 6,000 students were detained last August after riot police stormed Yonsei University to end the occupation of two teaching blocks by students taking part in an annual pro-Korean unification rally.
A Seoul court jailed or gave suspended jail sentences to 151 of the students.
North and South Korea are still technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce rather than a peace treaty.
Friday's unrest was also fuelled by anger at President Kim's apology for election spending abuses that was televised live, witnesses said.

Opposition parties allege that Kim's 1992 election was partly bankrolled by the scandal-ridden Hanbo Group and his disgraced predecessor, Roh Tae-woo. They say the campaign grossly exceeded legal spending limits.
